PLANKA already remembers which view a board was last put into, so this overlaps with what is there. We keep it in `sessionStorage` rather than in the database, and that difference is deliberate: with two windows open on the same board, one as a grid and one as a list, a setting stored per user makes each window change under the other's hands. `sessionStorage` keeps them independent. The stored choice also carries the context it was picked in, so a view chosen in the archive does not follow the board when you open it normally.

There is a second reason the column would be a problem regardless. A column that exists in Community and not in Pro breaks the upgrade path between the two, so every new column here costs work on the other side.

Closing this, but the instinct was right and the feature is there.

That's the auto-logout on inactivity, added in 2.2.0. Sessions end after a period without activity, with a warning shown before the sign-out. You can adjust the timeout or disable it in your user settings.

That also explains the pattern you describe: a session survives overnight if a tab stays active, and ends after a few minutes if it doesn't.

Closing as expected behavior — feel free to reopen if it still happens with the timeout disabled.

Thanks for this, and for the care that went into it. I am declining it, but I want to give you the actual reasons rather than a one liner.

The blocker is what happens on an existing instance. The migration leaves `due_date_expiration_notified_at` NULL on every row, so on the first sweep after upgrading, every card in the entire history with a past due date qualifies at once. On a server that has been running for a year that is hundreds of webhook deliveries in one go, fired sequentially with no limit. A backfill in the migration would fix that, setting the column for anything already overdue so only future expirations fire.

Two other things I found while reading it. The query filters on `isDueCompleted: { '!=': true }`, and that column is nullable with no default, so newly created cards have NULL there and `NULL != true` is not true in Postgres. The event would never fire for any card created after the upgrade. And there is no index on `due_date` or on the new column, so the watcher does a full scan of the card table every 60 seconds by default.

Beyond the bugs, we would rather not put a column on `card` for this. It is the busiest table we have, and a per card flag means the event cannot fire again if someone moves a due date into the future. A watermark holding the last swept timestamp would give the same guarantee without touching `card` at all.

If you want to take another run at it along those lines, I will review it properly and faster than this time.

PLANKA uses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH as a version format. We do not follow the SemVer spec and never have. Features being added and features being removed are both a minor bump here. PLANKA Pro is going from 2.4.4 to 2.5.0 with 150 additions, for the same reason. Nothing about 2.2.0 is a departure from how we have always versioned.

On upgrade documentation: the v2 guide exists because v1 to v2 required manual steps. 2.1 to 2.2 does not. Migrations run on boot, and the two things that do require action are in the release notes under "Breaking changes — read before updating": create a local admin user before updating if your only admin is SSO-based, and set passwords for the affected users afterwards to reactivate them. Node 24 for source installations is listed there too.

https://github.com/plankanban/planka/releases/tag/v2.2.0

The OIDC removal and the license behind it were discussed in #1754. That discussion is closed.

So there is nothing to withdraw. 2.2.0 and 2.2.1 stay.
